variants: Ameca (generation 2.6) on the product page. Engineered Arts sells Ameca Desktop, Ami Desktop, Azi Desktop and Mesmer on pages of their own, which this record does not cover.
availability_note: Engineered Arts' Ameca page has Book a Demo, Get a Quote and Rent buttons that open sales and rental inquiry forms, and the specifications say to configure a robot with "a customized Ameca quote". The pages state no price and no order path.

hardware.compute: An embedded robot PC, listed with RJ45 Ethernet, two Thunderbolt ports and two USB ports; no processor is named.
hardware.sensors: Two 8 MP cameras, one in each eye, two microphones, one in each ear, a 4-channel chest microphone, and 360-degree LiDAR safety sensors.
hardware.actuation: 61 actuated degrees of freedom: 27 in the head, 5 in the neck, 8 in the shoulders, 10 in the arms, 8 in the hands and 3 in the torso. The specifications list a height of 1870 mm, a weight of 62 kg and a 600 mm base.
hardware.power: Two mains power outlets at 110-240 V AC, 50/60Hz, 400W, and a robot power supply of 2 x 24Vdc, 200W.

developer_access: Engineered Arts' specifications list a control API of "REST, WebSocket, Python & Node.js SDKs" and AI integration through "Tritium AI. Default integrations with OpenAI ChatGPT, OpenAI Whisper, Amazon Poly. Custom integrations available." Its Ameca page says "Build, train, and deploy your AI models with ease." and that "Tritium AI is a cloud-based service that equips a humanoid robot with the ability to talk, listen, and generate responses using advanced AI technologies." Its Tritium AI page says the Pro agent platform lets you "connect MCP servers and external API integrations, choose from a range of LLMs or bring your own custom model". The model sits behind Tritium's cloud-based AI service rather than on the robot, and the developer documentation at docs.engineeredarts.co.uk is behind a login, so this record rests on the product and specification pages.
terms_note: Engineered Arts' Terms of Service, last updated August 2025, cover its website, products and services in general terms and are a site-level agreement, not terms of sale or software terms, so they are not classified. The specifications list a one-year warranty on parts and labor. No terms of sale or SDK licence were found at review time.
not_verified: The documented model route is Engineered Arts' own claim; the Atlas has not verified it. Every source is an Engineered Arts web page that the company can change at any time, and the pages render their text with JavaScript, so a link check sees no text to monitor.
